_why: SUBJECT-SPECIFIC level targets. This is the PACK side of the EDU engine/pack boundary: a new subject adds this file, it never edits the engine. The engine owns the CEFR ladder and the honesty rules; this file owns 'how good do I need to be, for THIS trip'.
_ladder_source: CEFR cumulative guided-learning-hour estimates, cross-read 2026-09-24 across CEFR/Spanish-school/FSI-derived tables (espanol.com, internationalenglishtest, lingualive, pcpcespanishschool). Ranges are quoted, never averaged into one fake number.

targets.label: Tourist zone — survival, not conversation
targets.why: Resort and expat zones (Sosúa, Cabarete, Punta Cana/Bávaro) run on English — hotels, bars and the venues already on file. A1 gets the taxi, the passport desk and the menu done. Not being fluent here costs nothing.

targets.label: Real city — conversational floor
targets.why: Santo Domingo and Santiago are not tourist zones. Outside the hotel desk and the airport, English thins out fast. A2 gets him understood but not conversing — B1 is the first level where a spontaneous exchange with a local is survivable. Cibao-region speech (Santiago, Moca, La Vega) drops the s hardest, so listening is the wall, not speaking.

targets.label: Two-week Thailand — get around politely
targets.why: Thai is FSI Category IV (~1,100 class hours). A fluent goal does not fit in the months before the trip, so the honest target is polite survival, not fluency.

default.label: No target resolved
default.why: No place in the trip data maps to a known zone. Refusing to invent a target rather than guessing one.
